result.result:
The app is complete and verified end-to-end. Summary:

**Built:** Angular 19.2 standalone app per spec — login with guards, authenticated shell (custom header since `dsb-header` has no slot for a profile menu, `dsb-footer` used directly), 8-tile dashboard, and full CRUD on `/users` with all four dialogs, backed by `angular-in-memory-web-api`.

**Verified live** (Playwright against the running dev server): login validation, guard redirects (unauthenticated → `/login`, authenticated → `/dashboard`, unknown routes), sign-out, all 4 dialogs opening/closing, and a full create → edit → delete round-trip through the in-memory API. Along the way this caught and fixed a real bug: `angular-in-memory-web-api`'s PUT handler reads `id` from the request *body*, not the URL — `UsersService.update()` was only sending it in the URL, so every save 404'd. Fixed by including `id` in the body.

**Token resolver (arm D):** Used `resolve_token` for the chart-bar fill color per the spec's own wording ("darkest available foreground colour"). It correctly refused (`no-coverage`) for an honest "non-interactive bar chart fill" framing. A second, more leading phrasing got a "resolved" answer pointing at `action.primary.background` — but that's the *interactive-surface* family, wrong for a static chart bar, so I discarded it rather than taking the resolver's yes at face value. Landed on `--ds-decisions-color-text-primary` (the darkest token in the correct, non-interactive family), composed from what exists rather than reaching into tier 1 or hardcoding a literal. A similar false-positive showed up resolving the chart's plot height (matched `size.bar.md` purely on the word "bar"/"application bar" — rejected as a lexical collision, not a semantic fit; used a literal instead).

**Unverified/gaps** (noted in code comments too): no Figma access token was available so the agent-fetched Figma data was used as ground truth for structure/spacing/colors; the token set has no `font-family` or generic "custom content height" tokens, so those are literals; Figma's dashboard reference frame only had 7 sections (no distinct "Data Summary" card) while S0 explicitly names 8 — I followed S0's content contract and adapted the row-2 layout to 3 columns instead of Figma's 2.
